title: Stream probe: deterministic retry contracts and backpressure diagnostics for async iterable <> WebStream interop
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a lightweight "stream probe" mechanism in the TypeScript SDK to enable deterministic retry contracts for transient network failures while keeping interoperability between AsyncIterator-based consumers and Web Streams. The probe provides liveness checks, explicit resumability tokens, and emits structured diagnostics for backpressure anomalies that surface in Console/Tracing. This ticket covers design, prototype, tests, and a gated rollout behind `enableStreamProbes` flag.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes an opt-in `createStreamProbe(stream, options)` helper that returns a wrapped async iterator and a companion WebReadableStream that mirror each other
On transient transport failure, consumers receive a clear RetryableError with a resumable offset token when the producer supports it
When probe is enabled, Console shows a `stream.probe` trace for each stream connection with backpressure metrics (avg queue, max latency, stall_count)
No regressions for existing streaming APIs when `enableStreamProbes=false` (defaults to false for GA)
Unit + integration tests covering: consumer cancellation, dual-consumer handoff, resumed sessions, and deliberate backpressure scenarios
technical_approach: Add a small control frame layer (JSON control envelopes) that is serialized into the same streaming channel as tokens but distinguishes probe/control from user tokens. The wrapper will: 1) maintain a monotonic `streamOffset` counter; 2) emit probe heartbeats with offset snapshots; 3) surface a `resumableToken` produced by the server (when supported); 4) record per-chunk queueing latency to surface backpressure metrics. On the TS side we provide two surfaces: an AsyncIterable wrapper (for existing consumers) and a ReadableStream wrapper (for browser Web Streams) that both share the same underlying controller. The adapter will implement deterministic semantics for retries: only offsets acknowledged by the probe heartbeat are eligible to resume, eliminating duplicate emission windows.
decisions: Use control envelopes vs. out-of-band control channel: chose same-channel control envelopes for compatibility with existing transports and to avoid extra connection negotiation
Expose probe as opt-in experimental flag rather than change default streaming contract
Server will be backward compatible: if resumableToken not present, SDK falls back to best-effort retry (idempotency recommended in caller)
Emit structured probe traces to Console via existing tracing hooks; do not create separate telemetry pipeline
tradeoffs: Pros: determinism for retries, improved visibility into backpressure, single implementation for async iter/WebStream interop
Cons: small increase in wire protocol complexity and per-token metadata; requires server-side support for resumable tokens for full guarantees
Alternatives considered: out-of-band control websocket (rejected for complexity) and adding explicit commit API (rejected for ergonomics)
tasks: Design control envelope schema and document in SDK API spec
Prototype wrapper (ts) that bridges AsyncIterator <-> ReadableStream using a single controller
Add unit tests for offset accounting, retry window enforcement, and cancellation semantics
Implement probe trace emitter (Console) and wire up to existing tracing hooks
Integration test with server-side proof-of-concept returning resumableToken
Create migration guide and examples for common patterns (single consumer, dual-consumer handoff, server resume)
Open PR and request reviews from runtime, SDK, and observability teams

test_plan: Unit tests for adapter invariants + property tests for offset monotonicity. Integration: run server POC with deterministic network injector to validate retry semantics across: brief TCP reset, slow consumer (backpressure), and dual-consumer handoff. Add e2e test in CI with `--enable-stream-probes` flag gated to experimental jobs.
rollout: Feature is behind `enableStreamProbes` flag. Start with internal dogfood for Redwood Console and two partner teams, collect metrics for 2 weeks. If no regressions, flip flag for beta customers and include explicit opt-in code samples. GA only after server-side `enableResumableOffsets` rollout and docs are published.
risk_mitigation: Default disabled to avoid changing current behavior
Add telemetry to detect any increased error-rate correlated with probes
Graceful fallback to best-effort retry when server lacks resumableToken
blockers: Runtime: full support for resumableToken (ENG-82012) is a hard dependency for deterministic resume
Console: lightweight schema for probe traces must be merged (observability team)
